title: Evidence-path symlink confinement

original_target.status_note: Recorded historical metadata is retained without claiming that this replay verifies the object or compares it with the published fix.

applicability: A repository validator accepts repository-relative evidence file references.
Referenced paths may contain file or directory symlinks.
Legitimate symlinks whose final target remains inside the repository must continue to work.
Containment must be checked after strict path resolution, including prefix-collision cases.
exclusions: Concurrent malicious path replacement after validation.
Network filesystems, mount-point attacks, or operating-system access-control enforcement.
Fresh bug discovery, cross-project transfer, demand validation, or effectiveness measurement.

prerequisites: Git with the baseline and published-fix commits available in local history
A filesystem and account permitted to create and follow symbolic links
replay.fixture_policy: Only inert files inside disposable replay-owned temporary directories are used.
replay.success_definition: PASS requires all essential cases to execute against both hash-verified production validators, all observations to match the committed matrix, the baseline escape defect to be observed, the fixed escape cases to be rejected, legitimate in-root cases to remain accepted, and temporary artifacts to be removed.

evidence_provenance.historical: PR #30 and the recorded original-target identity provide historical provenance. The replay does not require, load, execute, verify, or compare the original-target object.
evidence_provenance.runtime_verified_sources: Only the baseline and published-fix source identities are verified and executed by the replay.
evidence_provenance.new_replay_output: Each invocation independently records newly observed decisions from disposable fixtures. Output is not committed by this package.
evidence_provenance.separation: Committed expectations are emitted separately from observed_replay results.

limitations: The replay imports and calls the pinned production path validator but does not execute the complete Registry validation CLI.
A containment check can race with a later consumer if an attacker can replace filesystem components concurrently.
Only platforms on which the replay is actually run are observed; other platforms remain untested.
The case does not establish universal protection for every filesystem API or path representation.
